frequency_question: How often do central bank regulatory boards activate a non-zero countercyclical capital buffer when economic expansions mature over a multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes all G-7 jurisdictions with operational Basel III frameworks capable of setting a CCyB between 2016 and 2026. Excludes jurisdictions where macroprudential authority is split outside the central bank.

cases.name: Bank of England FPC UK CCyB activation
Bank of England FPC UK CCyB increase (subsequent cycle)
Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB activation
European Central Bank / National Authorities Eurozone CCyB implementations
US Federal Reserve Board CCyB setting (kept at 0%)
US Federal Reserve Board CCyB setting post-pandemic expansion (kept at 0%)

coverage_note: 6 named jurisdictions/episodes; representative of major advanced economy central bank behavior.
known_gaps: The US Federal Reserve has historically maintained a structural 0% default posture for the CCyB, differing from peer central banks in the UK and Europe which treat a positive neutral rate as standard practice.
skeleton: Peer central bank jurisdictions with independent macroprudential mandates evaluated during periods of sustained credit expansion.
multiplier: 4 active implementers globally (UK, EU, NZ, Canada) vs 1 non-implementer (US Fed) across comparable economic cycles.
validity_reason: Matches the exact resolution deadline of the forecast question.
